design:
D1 One shared `SettingsSection` / `SettingsRow` pair (`hub/ui/src/components/environment/SettingsSection.tsx`) serves project and per-agent settings; its `scope` eyebrow says which.

D2 The update body is derived from `ProjectSettings` with every field optional (`ProjectSettingsUpdate` in `hub/hub/api/v1/projects.py`), so a field cannot be accepted and then silently not written; the handler merges onto stored values with `exclude_unset` and validates the merged object.

D3 Steppers are removed in CSS (`hub/ui/src/index.css`), not by changing input types, so browser validation still applies.
lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: Per-project configuration moved out of the navigation rail into Environment sections. Those sections must read as complete, show what each setting does, never silently revert settings the surface did not know about, and say whether a save worked.

requirements.rationale: A section with few settings should still read as complete, and the operator should know whether it is project or agent configuration.
requirements.statement: Every configuration section SHALL open with its scope, its title and a short statement of what it governs.

requirements.rationale: Rows scan quickly and keep the explanation next to the control it explains.
requirements.statement: A configuration section SHALL present its settings as rows, each pairing a label and an explanation of the setting's effect with its control, separated by hairlines rather than each enclosed in a card.

requirements.rationale: A narrow column in a wide pane reads as unfinished.
requirements.statement: A configuration section SHALL fill the content region it is given, bounding text and controls to a readable measure without leaving a large unused region beside a narrow column.

requirements.rationale: Steppers invite accidental changes on hover and scroll; removing them must not remove validation.
requirements.statement: Numeric settings SHALL be typed, with no increment or decrement steppers in any browser engine, and SHALL keep their numeric constraints, an invalid value being refused with an explanation.

requirements.rationale: A save whose outcome is only in a log is a save the operator has to guess about.
requirements.statement: Saving a configuration section SHALL report success in the section, and a refused save SHALL state the reason in the section and keep the values the operator entered.

requirements.rationale: The note on an unmerged task sends the operator to settings to choose a branch; the control it names has to be there.
requirements.statement: The Settings section SHALL offer a main-branch control showing the project's chosen branch, offering the repository's detected branch as a one-click suggestion when none is chosen, and disabled with an explanation when the project is not a git repository.

requirements.rationale: A surface that must resend every setting can silently revert one it does not know about, which is how a save once cleared a project's checkpoint configuration.
requirements.statement: `PUT /projects/{id}/settings` SHALL accept a body naming only the fields being changed, treating an omitted field as unchanged and an explicit null as a clear, and SHALL apply cross-field validation to the merged result.

requirements.rationale: Budget changes made in Accounting were already in the project's history; the same change made in Settings must be too (F238).
requirements.statement: A settings save that changes at least one value SHALL persist a `project_settings_updated` event listing each changed field's previous and new value, and a save that changes nothing SHALL record nothing.

requirements.rationale: These references are not foreign keys, so the route is the only place a cross-project or deleted runner can be caught.
requirements.statement: A settings save naming a conversation-title runner or checkpoint runner that does not exist in this project SHALL be refused with 400 naming the runner ID.

requirements.rationale: The flat list of 18 is why the five gating rows are hard to find; nothing moves out of Settings.
requirements.statement: Environment > Settings MUST render its rows under headed groups in this order: Collaboration (agents may start flows, hop budget, per-turn delivery cap, agent budget), Integration (main branch, checks), Checkpointing (the checkpoint rows), Conversations (title mode, title runner), Project (name, directory, then delete set apart last).

requirements.rationale: Two editors for one field is the F237 shape; a Settings form holding a stale token_budget would overwrite a limit just set in Budgets.
requirements.statement: Environment > Settings MUST NOT render a token budget input and MUST NOT send token_budget in its save; its Collaboration group MUST link to Budgets, which stays the one editor.

requirements.rationale: The Hub checks it only in request_agent (api/v1/agents.py:2556); the current label promises a limit that does not exist (F557).
requirements.statement: Wherever agent budget is labelled (Settings and Overview), the text MUST say it caps how many agents the project may hold when an agent staffs a new one, and MUST NOT say it limits agents running at the same time.

requirements.rationale: The page and agents read one list; a job that has never been configured is still a job the operator can turn on.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/jobs MUST answer 200 with {"jobs": [...]}, one entry per registered job in registry order, each with key, title, description, trigger, enabled, runner_id and model; a job with no stored row MUST be listed with enabled false and runner_id and model null.

requirements.rationale: Same validation as the project settings route applies to conversation_title_runner_id today (projects.py:516-528).
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/jobs/{key} with any of enabled, runner_id and model MUST store them and answer the job as listed; an unknown key MUST answer 404, and a runner_id that is not one of this project's runners MUST answer 400 and change nothing.

requirements.rationale: Most title calls end before a spawn (already titled from this excerpt, F422); recording those would bury the firings that cost something.
requirements.statement: Every manager spawn MUST record one manager_job_fired event holding job, trigger, subject (for titles, the conversation id), runner_id, cli, model, outcome (written, empty or failed), detail (for titles, the title written), duration_ms and usage (null when the runner reports none). An exit before any spawn MUST record nothing.

requirements.rationale: A background agent whose work cannot be inspected is the hardest kind to trust (R5).
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/activity MUST answer {"firings": [...]}, newest first, at most limit entries (default 50, at most 200), optionally filtered by job.

requirements.rationale: turn_scheduler.schedule_agent and trigger_agent_directly gate on a running Run under the agent's name (conversation_titles.py:7-13).
requirements.statement: A manager firing MUST NOT create a Run row or hold an agent name, so it never makes an agent look busy or delays that agent's queue.

requirements.rationale: The settings body forbids unknown fields (projects.py:84), so an app window still running the old bundle would otherwise fail to save any project setting until reloaded; existing clients and tests keep their contract.
requirements.statement: GET and PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/settings MUST keep conversation_title_mode and conversation_title_runner_id: reading reports generate when the conversation-titles job is enabled and its runner_id, and writing sets the job's enabled flag and runner_id.

requirements.rationale: It runs on :8000's real database at its next restart; titles must keep behaving as configured, and rolling back must lose nothing that existed before.
requirements.statement: The migration MUST create manager_jobs and give every project whose conversation_title_mode is generate or whose conversation_title_runner_id is set a conversation-titles row (enabled exactly when the mode is generate, runner_id copied, model null); its downgrade MUST write each row's enabled flag and runner_id back to the project columns and drop the table.

requirements.rationale: A committed bundle reaches :8000's app on its next reload, possibly before its server restarts.
requirements.statement: The app's Environment MUST have a Manager section listing each job with an on/off control, a runner select and a model select, and below them the activity list; the Settings section MUST no longer show the conversation title controls. Where the Hub answers 404 for the manager routes, the section MUST say this Hub has no manager yet instead of failing.

in_scope: Presentation of Environment configuration sections (project and per-agent settings share it)
Typed numeric fields and save feedback
`PUT /projects/{id}/settings` partial-update semantics, runner references, and its history record
non_goals: What each individual setting means: owned by its capability (budgets, checkpointing, checks, conversation titles)
The settings resource as a whole, the main-branch setting's rules and detection, project identity, relocation and deletion: local-project-workspace
Re-attempting integrations when a main branch is named: approval-integration

summary: The project's configuration surface under Environment and the settings write behind it: how each section introduces itself, how settings are laid out as labelled rows, how saving reports its outcome, the main-branch control, that a change may name only the fields it changes, that a runner named in settings must belong to the project, and that a saved change is recorded in the project's history.
title: Project environment settings
